what_its_for: Cholestyramine is used to lower your 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) in your blood. It works by binding to bile acids in your gut so your body uses up cholesterol to make more bile acids. It may also be used to relieve itching caused by a liver condition where bile builds up in the body.
how_to_take: Cholestyramine comes as a powder that you must mix with liquid before swallowing — NEVER swallow it dry. Mix one packet or one level scoop with at least 2 to 6 ounces (60–180 mL) of water, juice, milk, or a non-carbonated beverage. Stir well until fully mixed and drink it all right away. You can also mix it into applesauce, soup, or crushed pineapple. Rinse your glass with a little more liquid and drink that too so you get the full dose. Take it with meals unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Because this medicine can block other drugs from being absorbed, take all your other medications at least 1 hour BEFORE or 4 to 6 hours AFTER taking cholestyramine.
dosing: The typical starting dose for adults is one packet or one scoop (4 grams of cholestyramine) taken 1 to 2 times per day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time. The usual maintenance dose is 2 to 4 packets or scoops per day, divided into 1 to 2 doses. Do not take more than 6 packets or scoops per day unless your doctor tells you to. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still close to your regular mealtime. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cholestyramine powder at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date printed on the box.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medications at the same time as cholestyramine, as it can prevent many drugs from being properly absorbed into your body. Always take other medicines at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after your cholestyramine dose. Avoid a high-fat diet, as it will work against the cholesterol-lowering effects of this medicine. Talk to your doctor before starting any new prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, or supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain or cramping, severe constipation that does not go away, black or tarry stools (which may indicate bleeding), unusual bleeding or bruising, sudden weight loss, signs of low vitamins such as muscle weakness, numbness, tingling, vision changes, or easy bruising, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to see a reduction in your cholesterol levels within 4 to 6 weeks of starting this medicine. To get the most benefit, keep taking it every day as prescribed, follow a heart-healthy low-fat diet, and get regular exercise. Cholesterol control is a long-term process, so this medication is usually taken for many years.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Cholestyramine is generally considered safe during pregnancy, but because it may reduce absorption of important vitamins (A, D, E, K, and folic acid), talk to your doctor about taking vitamin supplements. If you are breastfeeding, discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: This medicine can be used in children with high cholesterol under a doctor's supervision, but dosing will be adjusted based on your child's weight. Elderly patients: Older adults are more likely to experience constipation and vitamin deficiencies — make sure to drink plenty of fluids and tell your doctor about any side effects. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems before starting this medication.
